text.title: Outcome Based Roadmaps Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules every Outcome Based Roadmaps application must enforce. These are HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: Roadmap rows MUST be outcomes (e.g. 'Reduce trial→paid friction'); feature names as rows are rejected.
rule.rationale: Outcome-first preserves optionality on how to achieve the outcome.

rule.statement: ≤3 outcomes per quarter; >3 is rejected as overcommitment.
Each solution MUST have a delivery window expressed as month-range (e.g. 'May-June'); exact-date promises are rejected.
rule.rationale: Exact-date promises lock the team and erode trust on miss.

rule.statement: Every solution MUST carry confidence (high/med/low) with cited evidence (discovery touchpoint id, experiment id); uncited confidence is rejected.
rule.rationale: Uncited confidence defaults to 100% and inflates the plan.

rule.statement: Quarter-end review MUST cite which outcomes shipped, which slipped, and the next quarter's adjustment; un-reviewed roadmaps are rejected.
rule.rationale: Without quarter-end review the roadmap becomes a feature wishlist.

rule.statement: Every outcome title MUST parse as verb + metric + delta + timeframe (e.g. 'Reduce churn from 8% to 5% by EOQ2'); an outcome missing any of the four components is rejected.
rule.rationale: r1 rejects feature rows but still admits unmeasurable ones like 'delight users'; the four-component test is the binary check that makes an outcome scoreable and kill-signallable.

rule.statement: Every outcome MUST carry a falsifying kill signal of the form 'if metric < X by week N, kill this bet'; outcomes with no kill threshold are rejected.
rule.rationale: An outcome that cannot be falsified mid-quarter runs to the quarter boundary regardless of evidence, which is the expensive half of a wrong bet.

rule.statement: Every outcome MUST cite the URL of an existing analytics dashboard holding its baseline metric value, recorded before the roadmap is published.
rule.rationale: A target with no instrumented baseline cannot be reviewed at quarter-end, so r5 degrades into narrative.
